implemented_requirements.evidence: DIFFICULTIES dict in game.py defines Beginner (9x9,10), Intermediate (16x16,40), Expert (16x30,99) and GUI creates buttons for each level.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player uncovers cells by clicking on them
implemented_requirements.evidence: MinesweeperGUI.on_left bound to left‑click ("<Button-1>") calls game.reveal(r,c).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Numbers on uncovered cells indicate how many mines are adjacent
implemented_requirements.evidence: Cell.adjacent computed in place_mines; paint() displays cell.adjacent with color coding from NUM_COLORS.

implemented_requirements.requirement: If a mine is uncovered, the player loses
implemented_requirements.evidence: reveal() sets game_over=True when cell.mine; on_left shows "Boom!" message and updates status.

implemented_requirements.requirement: The game displays the board with updated markings after each move
implemented_requirements.evidence: update_all() called after each reveal/flag; paint() updates button text/background for each cell.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Include a flagging mechanism for suspected mines
implemented_requirements.evidence: toggle_flag() in Minesweeper toggles Cell.flagged; on_right() bound to right‑click calls toggle_flag and repaints.
paint() sets FLAG_BG background and "F" text for flagged cells; different colors for wrong flags after game over.

judge.summary: The submitted code provides a complete, runnable Minesweeper implementation with three difficulty levels, click‑to‑reveal, numbered hints, loss on mine, automatic board updates, and a functional flagging system with clear visual cues. All core requirements are satisfied and the program is likely executable in a standard Python environment with Tkinter.
